### 3.2 Part V Failure Mode Self-Audit (`FM-17`–`FM-21`)

| Code | Failure Mode Name | Broken Habit / Symptom | Mathematical Root Cause | Mandatory Defensive Guard & Chapter Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`FM-17`** | **Stale Johnson Potentials & Un-Saturated Negative Cycles** | Updating $\pi_v \gets \pi_v + d_v$ only along the augmenting path $P$, forgetting to negate reverse arc costs `cost[id ^ 1] = -cost[id]`, or running SPFA/Dijkstra directly on a cyclic graph with negative-cost edges (`Drill 1.1`). | Leaving $\pi_v$ un-updated on off-path reachable nodes violates $c^{\pi'}(u, v) = c^\pi(u, v) + d_u - d_v \ge 0$; negative cycles cause infinite SPFA loops unless pre-saturated. | Update $\pi_v \gets \pi_v + d_v$ for **every node $v$ with $d_v < \infty$** after each Dijkstra; on cyclic networks with $c(e) < 0$, pre-saturate $f(e) = u(e)$, adjust $M(u), M(v)$, and add reverse arc $(v \to u, u(e), -c(e) > 0)$ ([Ch 17 §17.1–17.3](../chapters/ch17-mcmf-foundations-potentials-slope-negative-cycles.qmd)). |
| **`FM-18`** | **Concave Fixed-Charge Parallel Arc Trap & Un-Complemented Tournament Triples** | Splitting a concave or fixed-charge cost $\Phi(f) = F_e \cdot [f > 0] + b_e f$ ($F_e > 0$) into parallel unit arcs (`Drill 1.2`), or trying to count transitive tournament triples directly without complementing via out-degrees $d_i^+$. | When $\Delta\Phi(1) > \Delta\Phi(2)$, MCMF routes the first unit of flow along the cheaper second arc ($b_e$), bypassing the first arc ($F_e + b_e$); transitive triples involve 3 edges, whereas non-transitive triples depend only on $\sum_i \binom{d_i^+}{2}$. | **Always verify convexity** $\Delta\Phi(1) \le \Delta\Phi(2) \le \dots \le \Delta\Phi(U)$ before unrolling parallel arcs; for tournaments, use Kendall–Babington Smith $T_{\text{trans}} = \binom{N}{3} - \sum_{i=1}^N \binom{d_i^+}{2}$ with marginal costs $0, 1, 2, \dots$ ([Ch 18 §18.1–18.4](../chapters/ch18-convex-marginal-splitting-degree-penalties-tournaments.qmd)). |
| **`FM-19`** | **Off-by-One Interval Differencing ($l_j \to r_j$ vs. $l_j \to r_j + 1$) & Nested Subtree Double-Subtraction** | Wiring closed integer interval $[l_j, r_j]$ as $l_j \to r_j$ instead of $l_j \to r_j + 1$ (`Drill 1.3`), or subtracting *all* constrained descendants instead of only *highest* constrained descendants in tree differencing (`#231`). | In $\Delta E_i = E_i - E_{i-1}$, an indicator covering $i \in \{l_j, \dots, r_j\}$ has $+1$ at $i = l_j$ and $-1$ at $i = r_j + 1$; subtracting nested descendants $w \prec v \prec u$ subtracts $E_w$ multiple times. | For closed integer intervals $[l_j, r_j]$, always wire $l_j \leftrightarrow r_j + 1$ (with dummy node $N+1$); for half-open $[s_j, t_j)$, wire $\text{id}(s_j) \leftrightarrow \text{id}(t_j)$; on trees, subtract only $v \in \text{ch}^*(u)$ with $\text{anc}(\text{parent}(v)) = u$ ([Ch 19 §19.1–19.3](../chapters/ch19-k-interval-coverage-equation-difference-method.qmd)). |
| **`FM-20`** | **Merged Dirty/Clean Inventory Nodes & Forward Queue-Slot Indexing** | Using a single node $v_i$ per day in `餐巾计划` (`Drill 1.4`), or indexing machine queue slots *forward* from the start of shift instead of *backward* from the end (`#227` `修车` / `美食节`). | A single day node lets dirty inflow from $S \to v_i$ exit directly to clean demand $v_i \to T$ at cost $0$; forward position $q$ delays $k_j - q + 1$ jobs where $k_j$ is unknown beforehand. | Split day $i$ into **Dirty Supply $D_i$** ($S \to D_i$) and **Clean Demand $C_i$** ($C_i \to T$); index machine slots by **reverse position $p \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ from the end** with static cost $p \cdot T_{i,j}$, and spawn slot $(j, p+1)$ lazily when $(j, p)$ saturates ([Ch 20 §20.2–20.3](../chapters/ch20-cycle-covers-dynamic-scheduling-resource-reuse-hubs.qmd)). |
| **`FM-21`** | **LP Dual Sign Inversion & Non-TU Odd-Cycle Half-Integrality** | Mixing $\ge$ and $\le$ constraints when taking the LP dual of path-crashing or covering LPs (`Drill 1.5`), or assuming vertex-edge incidence LP relaxations are integral on general graphs with odd cycles. | Flipping a primal inequality sign turns a $[-1, +1]$ conservation column into $[+1, +1]$; odd cycles $C_{2k+1}$ have submatrix determinant $\pm 2$, producing $1/2$-integral optima. | Normalize all primal constraints to standard form before dualizing so each potential difference $\pi_v - \pi_u$ produces exact Kirchhoff conservation $\delta^+(v) - \delta^-(v) = 0$; verify Total Unimodularity (bipartite / network matrix) before asserting LP integrality ([Ch 21 §21.1–21.3](../chapters/ch21-lp-duality-totally-unimodular-matrices-polymatroids.qmd)). |

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Self-Audit Rapid Check — 5 Diagnostic Questions (Verify Before Proceeding)"}

1. **(`FM-17`)** In an MCMF network with negative edge costs on a DAG (`#226` `CF 164C`, `#230` `CF 818G`), why can you initialize $\pi_v$ in $O(V + E)$ without SPFA, and why does that fail if the initial graph contains a directed cycle?
   - *Check*: On a DAG, topological order guarantees no cycles exist and computes shortest distances $d_v$ in a single linear pass; on a cyclic graph, a negative cycle has $-\infty$ shortest path and must be eliminated via mandatory arc pre-saturation ($f(e) = u(e)$).
2. **(`FM-18`)** Given edge cost $\Phi(f) = c_e \cdot f^2$ vs. $\Phi(f) = c_e \cdot \sqrt{f}$ for integer flow $f \in \{0, 1, \dots, U\}$ ($c_e > 0$), which one can be compiled into $U$ parallel unit-capacity MCMF arcs?
   - *Check*: Only $\Phi(f) = c_e f^2$ ($\Delta\Phi(k) = c_e(2k-1)$ is strictly increasing). The square-root cost $\Phi(f) = c_e \sqrt{f}$ has strictly decreasing marginals ($\sqrt{1}-0 > \sqrt{2}-\sqrt{1} > \dots$, **concave**!), so MCMF would pick the $U$-th arc before the $1$-st arc.
3. **(`FM-19`)** In Consecutive Equation Differencing $\Delta E_i = E_i - E_{i-1}$ (`Ch 19.2`), how does changing a point coverage constraint from $\ge A_i$ to an interval $[A_i, B_i]$ modify the spine arc between $i$ and $i+1$?
   - *Check*: Instead of an unbounded slack variable $y_i \ge 0$ (capacity $\infty$ on $i+1 \to i$), the slack variable is bounded by $y_i \in [0, B_i - A_i]$, which simply changes the capacity of the backward spine arc $i+1 \to i$ from $\infty$ to $B_i - A_i$!
4. **(`FM-20`)** In `Luogu P2050 [NOI2012] 美食节` ($N \le 40$ dishes, total orders $P = \sum p_i \le 800$, $M \le 100$ chefs), why do we not pre-allocate all $M \times P = 80,000$ chef-slot vertices before running MCMF?
   - *Check*: Because for any chef $j$, $\text{Slot}(j, p)$ has strictly smaller cost $p \cdot T_{i,j}$ than $\text{Slot}(j, p+1)$ for *every* dish $i$. Thus Dijkstra will never augment through $\text{Slot}(j, p+1)$ until $\text{Slot}(j, p)$ is saturated! Lazily adding $\text{Slot}(j, p+1)$ (and its $N$ incoming dish edges) only when $\text{Slot}(j, p)$ is matched keeps the active graph at $\le M + P = 900$ slot nodes instead of $80,000$.
5. **(`FM-21`)** After solving a Maximum-Weight Bipartite Perfect Matching via MCMF (`#228` `Luogu P3967`), how do you determine in $O(N^2)$ time which matched edges belong to *every* optimal perfect matching?
   - *Check*: Build the zero-reduced-cost residual subgraph $G_{f^*}^{(0)}$ containing all positive-capacity residual arcs with $c(u, v) + \pi_u - \pi_v = 0$, and run Tarjan's SCC algorithm; a matched edge $(L_i, R_j) \in M^*$ is mandatory iff $\operatorname{scc}(L_i) \neq \operatorname{scc}(R_j)$ in $G_{f^*}^{(0)}$.

::::

## 4. Readiness Bridge to Part VI: Graph Sparsification, Blossom Matching, Simulated MCMF & Isotonic Regression (`Ch 22`–`Ch 24`)

In **Part V (`Ch 17`–`Ch 21`)**, you mastered the art of compiling complex algebraic, scheduling, inventory, and LP duality structures into polynomial-size Min-Cost Max-Flow networks. As you enter the final frontier of the textbook—**Part VI (`Ch 22`–`Ch 24`)**—the central question shifts from *"Can this problem be modelled as a flow or MCMF network?"* to **"What do we do when the explicit flow or MCMF graph is still too large ($N \le 2 \cdot 10^5, E = \Theta(N^2)$) or non-bipartite?"**

1. **From Relay/Manhattan Hubs (`Ch 20.4`) to Data-Structure-Accelerated Flow Graphs & Non-Bipartite Blossom Matching ([Chapter 22](../chapters/ch22-ds-accelerated-flow-graphs-blossom-matching.qmd))**:
   - In `#230` (`CF 818G Four Melodies`), you used value and modulo-$7$ relay chains to compress $O(N^2)$ transitions down to $O(N)$ edges.
   - In `Ch 22`, when transitions target arbitrary 1D intervals $[L_i, R_i]$, 2D rectangles, subtree/path ranges, or XOR prefixes ($N \le 5 \cdot 10^4$), you will replace explicit relay chains with **Segment Tree `In-Tree` / `Out-Tree` hubs, Persistent Trees, KD-Trees, and 0-1 Tries** (`数据结构优化建图`), reducing $\Theta(N^2)$ edge counts to $O(N \log N)$. In the second half of `Ch 22`, you will break the bipartite parity barrier (`FM-21` odd cycles!) using **Edmonds' Blossom Algorithm (`带花树`)** and **Tutte Matrix Pfaffians**.
2. **From Successive Shortest Paths & Convex Marginals (`Ch 17`–`Ch 18`) to Simulated MCMF & Regret-Greedy Heaps ([Chapter 23](../chapters/ch23-simulated-mcmf-regret-greedy-heap-segtree.qmd))**:
   - In `Ch 17`–`Ch 20`, each augmenting path on a 1D temporal spine (`#226` `CF 164C`, `#230` `CF 802C`, `餐巾计划`) either selects a fresh pairing $(i, j)$ or traverses a **backward residual arc** to cancel an earlier decision and splice two paths together.
   - In `Ch 23` (`模拟费用流`), when $N \le 5 \cdot 10^5$, you will simulate those exact residual augmenting paths **without ever building the flow graph**—replacing Dijkstra with **Regret Priority Queues (`反悔贪心` / `反悔堆`)**, **Linked-List 3-for-2 Residual Cancellation** (`种树` / `数据备份`), and **Segment Trees Maintaining Minimum-Cost Residual Cycles**.
3. **From Slope Convexity & LP Duality (`Ch 17.2`, `Ch 21`) to WQS Binary Search, Tree Simulated Flow & $L_p$ Isotonic Regression ([Chapter 24](../chapters/ch24-isotonic-regression-matroid-intersection-synthesis.qmd))**:
   - Because the minimum-cost flow function $C(F)$ is convex (`Ch 17.2`), constraining the total flow to $F = K$ at $N = 5 \cdot 10^5$ can be dualized via **WQS Binary Search (Aliens Trick)**: binary search a Lagrangian slope penalty $\lambda$ per unit of flow and solve the unconstrained simulated flow problem in $O(N \log N)$ per step!
   - Finally, combining Part III's Coarea Level-Set Cuts (`Ch 13`) with Part V's LP Duality (`Ch 21`) and Part IV's Subtree Differencing (`#231` `CF 1061E`) culminates in **Dykstra/CDQ Divide-and-Conquer for $L_p$ Isotonic Regression (`保序回归`, 国家集训队 2018)** and **Weighted Matroid Intersection**.

### 4.1 Part V Algebraic-to-Graph Compilation Cheat Sheet

Keep this quick-reference compilation table beside you as you transition into Part VI and the Grandmaster Synthesis Capstones:

| Modelling Archetype | Algebraic / Dual Formulation | Mechanical Graph Compilation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Negative-Cost Arc on Cyclic Graph** (`Ch 17.3`, `Drill 1.1`) | $f(e) = u(e) - \tilde{f}_{\text{rev}}(e)$ for $c(e) < 0$ | Pre-pay $u(e) c(e)$, shift balances $M(v) \mathrel{+}= u(e), M(u) \mathrel{-}= u(e)$, add reverse arc $v \xrightarrow{u(e),\; -c(e) > 0} u$ |
| **Separable Convex Cost $\Phi(f)$** (`Ch 18.1`, `Drill 1.2`) | $\Phi(f) = \Phi(0) + \sum_{k=1}^f \Delta\Phi(k)$ with $\Delta\Phi(1) \le \dots \le \Delta\Phi(U)$ | $U$ parallel unit-capacity arcs $u \xrightarrow{\text{cap } 1,\; \text{cost } \Delta\Phi(k)} v$ ($k = 1, \dots, U$) |
| **Tournament Transitive Triples** (`Ch 18.4`) | $\max \left[\binom{N}{3} - \sum_{i=1}^N \binom{d_i^+}{2}\right]$ | Match arc $e \to \{u, v\}$ (win receiver) and split $v \to T$ into parallel unit arcs of costs $0, 1, 2, \dots, N-2$ |
| **Doubly-Bounded Interval Coverage** (`Ch 19.2`, `Drill 1.3`) | $\Delta E_i = E_i - E_{i-1}$ on $\sum_{j: i \in [l_j, r_j]} x_j - y_i = A_i$, $y_i \in [0, B_i - A_i]$ | Interval arc $l_j \xrightarrow{(1, -w_j)} r_j + 1$, backward slack spine $i + 1 \xrightarrow{(B_i - A_i,\; 0)} i$, demand balance $A_i - A_{i-1}$ |
| **Two-Tree Subtree Quotas** (`Ch 19.3`, `#231`) | $c(u) = k_u - \sum_{v \in \text{ch}^*(u)} k_v$ over disjoint region $R(u)$ | Bipartite MCMF: $S \xrightarrow{(c_1(u), 0)} R_1(u)$, $R_2(w) \xrightarrow{(c_2(w), 0)} T$, vertex $i$ as $R_1(\text{anc}_1(i)) \xrightarrow{(1, -a_i)} R_2(\text{anc}_2(i))$ |
| **Dirty/Clean Multi-Period Inventory** (`Ch 20.2`, `Drill 1.4`) | Split day $i$ into dirty generation $D_i$ and clean consumption $C_i$ | $S \xrightarrow{(r_i, 0)} D_i$, $C_i \xrightarrow{(r_i, 0)} T$, holdover $D_i \xrightarrow{(\infty, 0)} D_{i+1}$, fresh buy $S \xrightarrow{(\infty, p)} C_i$, laundry $D_i \xrightarrow{(\infty, c_{\text{wash}})} C_{i+d}$ |
| **Multi-Machine Total Waiting Time** (`Ch 20.3`, `#227`) | $\sum_{p=1}^{k_j} p \cdot T_{i_{k_j - p + 1},\, j}$ ($p$-th from end of machine $j$) | Bipartite matching $\text{Task}_i \xrightarrow{(1,\; p \cdot T_{i,j})} \text{Slot}(j, p)$; spawn $\text{Slot}(j, p+1)$ lazily when $\text{Slot}(j, p)$ saturates |
| **Mandatory Edges in Optimal Matching** (`Ch 17`, `#228`) | $e \in \bigcap M^* \iff e^{\text{rev}}$ lies on no $c^\pi = 0$ cycle in $G_{f^*}$ | Run Tarjan SCC on $G_{f^*}^{(0)} = \{a \in G_{f^*} : c_{f^*}(a) > 0, c(a) + \pi_u - \pi_v = 0\}$; check $\operatorname{scc}(L_i) \ne \operatorname{scc}(R_j)$ |
| **Complete Bipartite Flow at $N = 2 \cdot 10^5$** (`Ch 21`, `#232`) | Fix $k = |L \cap S_{\text{cut}}| \in \{0, \dots, N\}$ in Min-Cut Dual | Sort $A_i$ and $\lfloor C_j / B_j \rfloor$; evaluate $\min_{0 \le k \le N} \big(\sum_{i=1}^{N-k} A_{(i)} + \sum_{j=1}^M \min(k B_j, C_j)\big)$ in $O((N+M)\log(N+M))$ |
